claims.claim_text: William J. Donovan's immediate pre-OSS assignment was Coordinator of Information.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: DOJ and Columbia chronologies place Donovan as Coordinator of Information from July 1941 until the office became OSS in June 1942.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Exact full name, commissioned Army context, and leadership chronology identify the indexed person at high confidence.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit institutional succession from COI to OSS.
claims.match_notes: COI is classified as a government assignment, not a civilian employer.

claims.claim_text: Donovan's last documented civilian employer before COI was Donovan, Leisure, Newton & Irvine.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Columbia identifies Donovan as the firm's founder in 1929 and places his COI appointment in July 1941.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The distinctive exact name and continuous Columbia biography support the identity match.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly bounded before the intervening COI government assignment.
claims.match_notes: The historical firm name is preserved and not replaced by a modern successor.

claims.claim_text: Carl F. Eifler entered COI from command of K Company, 35th Infantry Regiment.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Army biography places Eifler on active duty commanding K Company in 1941 and then assigned to COI in 1942.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Exact full name and matching colonel, Army, and OSS context support a high-confidence match.
claims.match_notes: The military unit is not treated as a civilian employer.

claims.claim_text: Eifler's last documented civilian employer before active Army duty was the U.S. Customs Service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official Army biography describes his undercover customs work in Mexico before his early-1941 call to active duty.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The distinctive name and detailed Army chronology align with the indexed colonel.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly bounded before active military service.
claims.match_notes: This is classified as civilian federal employment, not a military assignment.

claims.claim_text: David K. E. Bruce moved to OSS from his American Red Cross post in Great Britain.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: In his oral history, Bruce says he became the Red Cross chief representative in 1940 and then moved to OSS in 1941.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Exact indexed first and middle initial, distinctive surname, and four-year OSS chronology support a high-confidence match.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicitly immediate in Bruce's first-person chronology.
claims.match_notes: The expanded middle names are retained as a documented variant, not substituted for the index spelling.

claims.claim_text: Bruce's last documented civilian employer before OSS and wartime Army service was the American Red Cross.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Bruce's own chronology places the Red Cross role in 1940, OSS entry in 1941, and Army service beginning in 1942.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The same first-person account supplies the matching OSS and Army chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicitly the final named civilian organization before OSS.
claims.match_notes: Earlier business and farming are not collapsed into this named employer field.

claims.claim_text: Frank G. Wisner entered OSS from the Office of Naval Intelligence.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: CIA's official history dates Wisner's ONI service to 1941-43 and his OSS service to 1943-46.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Exact full name, matching lieutenant commander rank, Navy note, and OSS history support a high-confidence match.
claims.match_notes: ONI is a military assignment, not a civilian employer.

claims.claim_text: Wisner's last documented civilian employer before Naval service was Carter, Ledyard & Milburn.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The CIA history identifies him as a partner in the firm and then dates his Naval service from 1941.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The same official biography connects the distinctive indexed person to the firm, ONI, and OSS.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly bounded before the intervening ONI assignment.
claims.match_notes: The historical firm is not given a modern LLP suffix.

claims.claim_text: John A. Bross entered OSS after being called to active duty in the Army Air Forces.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Army Intelligence Center history states that Bross received a reserve commission, entered active duty, and was recruited into OSS.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Exact full name and middle initial, commissioned Army chronology, and OSS London service support a high-confidence match.
claims.match_notes: The official source resolves the indexed rank omission without inferring from the service number.

claims.claim_text: Bross's last documented civilian occupation before military service was private legal practice in Manhattan.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official Army history says Bross practiced law in Manhattan until 1942, before his active-duty call.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The same official biography supplies the matching full name and wartime chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly bounded immediately before active military service.
claims.match_notes: No firm is named, so this is modeled as self-employment rather than an invented employer.

claims.claim_text: California Institute of Technology is the best-supported probable immediate pre-OSS affiliation for Kermit Roosevelt Jr.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: CIA history places Roosevelt's Caltech teaching after Harvard and before wartime OSS service; a 1940 Caltech bulletin confirms the appointment.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Exact name with suffix, presidential-family note, Caltech chronology, and commissioned Army context support a high-confidence match.
claims.temporal_assessment: Probable rather than explicit immediacy because the sources do not exclude a short intervening affiliation.
claims.match_notes: The profile visibly qualifies the temporal conclusion.

claims.claim_text: Caltech is the last documented civilian employer currently identified before Roosevelt's OSS service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The institutional directory confirms his Caltech faculty role, and CIA history places that role before OSS.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The distinctive name, suffix, and institutional chronology align with the index.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar and probably last civilian, but the exact departure date remains unconfirmed.
claims.match_notes: The claim is excluded from default high-confidence employer analytics.

claims.claim_text: S. Lane Faison Jr. transferred to OSS from the United States Naval Reserve in 1945.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Williams states that Faison was transferred as a naval reservist to OSS and separately records his lieutenant commander rank.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Indexed full name, matching lieutenant commander rank and Navy note, and distinctive art-history assignment support a high-confidence match.
claims.match_notes: The source's S. Lane Faison Jr. form is retained as a name variant.

claims.claim_text: Faison's last documented civilian employer before Naval and OSS service was Williams College.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Williams documents his faculty service beginning in 1936, department chair role from 1940, and subsequent wartime Naval Reserve and OSS service.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The institutional biography aligns with the indexed full name, rank, and branch.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly bounded before the intervening Naval Reserve assignment.
claims.match_notes: Williams is treated as an employer, not merely as Faison's alma mater.

claims.claim_text: Peter M. F. Sichel entered OSS from an Army Medical Corps assignment.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: CIA's institutional review says Sichel enlisted after Pearl Harbor, was assigned to the Medical Corps, and was then interviewed for OSS.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact four-part indexed name and CIA biography support this fuller-name entity at high confidence.
claims.match_notes: The claim is not copied to the adjacent shorter-name entity because the service numbers differ.

claims.claim_text: The Peter M. Sichel row remains separate from the adjacent Peter M. F. Sichel row pending direct service-number linkage.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NARA prints adjacent same-box rows with different full service numbers; CIA notes one Peter Sichel served first enlisted and later under a direct commission.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The shorter name and shared box make duplication plausible, but neither reviewed source links both indexed service numbers to one person.
claims.temporal_assessment: Identity ambiguity prevents assigning the fuller-name entity's pre-OSS affiliation to this row.
claims.match_notes: The two source rows and person entities are deliberately not merged.
